claim: A multi-line claim breaks the inbox format: a claim line `note: ...` comes before the real note line and AC-12 takes the first one; a claim line starting with `###` makes a fake entry; render must collapse whitespace in claim, title and id.

Frame item 1 promises each ticket with a section waiting for stapel ok, but the Term narrows it to next actions write-page or confirm; a provisional section during the build and a ticket with an owed finding (decide returns ask-human first) get no confirmation entry.
A note that starts with `-` (`- fix it`) is parsed by clap as an option: stapel answer exits 2 and the button fails; no criterion or Inputs row covers it.

The person types a note (dirty buffer) and the server rewrites inbox.md on disk; notes typed for other findings can be lost and the editor may show a conflict; the reload is not promised and the stand records only one answer.

AC-7 lists fewer refusals than plan_triage and journal_ticket have (legacy or unreadable state.json, a Problem line in findings.jsonl, no git user name); a closed ticket is in the test row but has no reason or exit code.
match_branch passes when the checkout has no branch ticket: stapel answer on main writes into main's stale copy of a ticket that lives in a worktree; the case is undefined and untested.

The External states table skips dimensions: detached HEAD worktrees, paths with spaces, GIT_* environment, the same key in two worktrees in another case, the claude-code hook environment against the Bash shell, case-insensitive file systems and the permissions of inbox.md.
Sort by key is undefined (STP-10 before STP-9 as strings); a finding id `confirmation` collides with the confirmation heading; missing claim, stage or round fields and the title source have no rule.
`inbox: 1 decisions wait` for one decision; the run label of STP-39 puts the whole note into the message and the log.
The source of the waiting ids of AC-2 is not named; config order is only in the test plan; AC-5's failing next has no test case.

AC-12 and AC-14 both promise the rewrite, so step 11's RED does not fail for answers; AC-14 has no argument lists; AC-13's InvalidParams text of STP-39 names ticket.md or page.md, wrong for an inbox URI.
Proposal: a note from stdin or --note-file; a stapel ok button on confirmation entries.
AC-11 does not say which entry a range that spans two entries, or the ticket heading line, belongs to.
